doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Elvis Presley, the Beatles and Abbey Lincoln's remark
summary: He recalls his band's dislike of Elvis, Tony Spargo's reaction, and Abbey Lincoln's claim in the Burns series about the Beatles.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I mean I look back, I look at him now and I almost shed a tear. When he first came out I remember I was working with Tony Spargo who was the original drummer with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, right? And he says, “Oh y’all are just jeal—” he had a southern, New Orleans accent, he said, “y’all are just jealous of him because he’s got such a pretty face.” But when he first came out I didn’t think very much of his music at all, in fact we hated it. It was gyrations and obscene, and there we are, very staid guys, we’re going to play the music correctly and properly. And what he was doing was sort of obscene. Then after him The Beatles, that was the end of it. And I think the audience was crazy. It was Abbey Lincoln, I saw her, “The Beatles were brought to America by the Brits to undermine the black man’s music and economy.” That’s deep shit boy. And I heard that on a jazz show. Ken Burns presents Jaaaaz. That was done, I think it was Abbey Lincoln that said that.
You remember that? She accused the Brits of sending these guys over to kill the black market for R&B.
